findings.evidence: Page 27 cites the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next context window as "Appendix A §10", while page 51 cites the same model card as "(source: model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10)".
findings.issue: Two different reference forms ("Appendix A §10" and "A.10") point at the same appendix location, and neither matches the appendix's own stated numbering convention from the Preface ("Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N"). Under that convention "A.10" reads as a figure, but the List of Figures stops at A.5.
findings.fix_instruction: Pick one form for appendix sections (the Preface's letter-suffix form, e.g. "§ 10A", or a plain "A §10") and apply it at both page 27 and page 51; do not use the A.N figure-style token for a section.

findings.evidence: Table 3-3 — Parameter and KV cache arithmetic: dense 70B vs MoE (8×7B class) lists the row "KV cache per request (9.2K ctx, FP16)" with the MoE column value "~1.2 GB" and derivation "9,200 × 0.131 MB/token ≈ 1.20 GB". But the same chapter's §3.3.3 text states: "KV per token = 2 × 32 × 8 × 128 = 65,536 B = 0.0655 MB/token at 8-bit, so 9,200 × 0.0655 MB ≈ 0.60 GB (≈1.2 GB at FP16)". The derivation in Table 3-3 says 0.131 MB/token, which is the FP16 rate, but the text immediately above it labels 0.0655 MB/token as the 8-bit rate and 1.2 GB as the FP16 figure — so the table row's per-token constant (0.131 MB) is FP16, not 8-bit, while the neighbouring 8-bit row derives 0.0655 MB from the same geometry. Both are internally consistent per-row, but a reader scanning the two rows sees 0.131 MB and 0.0655 MB for what the text calls the same 'challenger's own 32L/4096H GQA (8 KV-heads × 128)' geometry without the table stating that 0.131 is the FP16 figure and 0.0655 the 8-bit figure; the row labels carry the precision, so this is a presentation-clarity defect rather than an arithmetic error.
findings.issue: Table 3-3's two KV rows for the MoE column use per-token constants (0.131 MB vs 0.0655 MB) that differ by exactly 2x (FP16 vs 8-bit) but the table does not label the precision of the per-token constant in the derivation cell, unlike Table 7-1 which explicitly states '8-bit here means FP8 (one byte per K/V element), not a block-scaled INT8 scale-offset layout'.
findings.fix_instruction: In Table 3-3, add the precision qualifier to each per-token constant in the derivation cells (e.g. '0.131 MB/token at FP16' and '0.0655 MB/token at 8-bit, raw byte-halving'), matching the labelling discipline already used in Table 7-1 and in the §3.3.3 prose.

findings.evidence: Table 4-2's canonical-scenario ledger row "Execution occupancy" gives "~86 / ~344 requests (at Wexec ≈ 8.6 s, where Wexec = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode = 8.58 s, shown as 8.6 s throughout the book; upper bound — Wexec contains the 1.08 s two-term prefill cap, so B_other is not deducted)". §4.3's Canonical Workload box repeats "Mean request service time (planning headline — not used for occupancy) ~10 s" and the execution-occupancy note: "The occupancy service time is Wexec ≈ 8.6 s: prefill + decode, shown as 8.58 s in Table 4-2. It excludes the ~120 ms retrieval term." Chapter 2 §2.3 states the same occupancy: "the capacity question — how many such hosts to absorb λ = 40 rps, where in-flight concurrency Lexec = λWexec ≈344 at the ~8.6 s service time (that occupancy is derived in Ch 4 §3 and carried in Table 4-2)". Recomputing: 40 rps × 8.58 s = 343.2 → ~344 ✓; 10 rps × 8.58 s = 85.8 → ~86 ✓. But Chapter 4 §4.6 uses the per-host slot screen as '86 in-flight ÷ 17 slots = 5.06' and Chapter 17's host count ⌈344/17⌉ = 21. With Wexec shown as '8.6 s' in the ledger and '8.58 s' in the prose, a reader recomputing 40 × 8.6 = 344 exactly, and one recomputing 40 × 8.58 = 343.2, get the same headline; however Chapter 4 §4.3's own cost-basis arithmetic elsewhere in the chapter uses a distinct third number: 'the same fleet is ~$3.33 per 1K requests (hour-matched, active-hours basis, 6-host average at the ~10 rps average)' derived from '10 × 3,600 × 8 × 260/12 = 6,240,000' — while the per-request decode figure quoted repeatedly for the same workload is '300 × 25 ms = 7.5 s'. The 8.58 s figure therefore embeds the 1.08 s prefill cap (which Table 4-2 flags as 'NOT a feasible deployed prefill target', since budget_prefill ≤ 1.08 s − B_other), so every occupancy, host-count and $/1K figure in Chs 4, 6, 8, 16, 17 and 20 inherits an upper-bound service time that the book itself says cannot be met in deployment.
findings.issue: The service time Wexec = 8.58 s used as the denominator for every Little's-law occupancy, host-count and per-1K-request figure book-wide is built on the 1.08 s prefill figure that Table 4-2 explicitly labels 'two-term-only upper cap, NOT a feasible deployed prefill target' with 'B_other' (admission/queue and tokenization/transfer) not deducted; the upper-bound status is noted on the Table 4-2 row and in the Canonical Workload box, but the derived occupancies (~86/~344), the 17-slot host screen (⌈344/17⌉ = 21) and the cost-per-1K figures do not repeat it, so a reader can carry them into a sizing deck as measured quantities.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the 'upper-bound, B_other not deducted' qualifier inline to the execution-occupancy row's downstream consumers — at minimum where ~86/~344 is first used for the 17-slot host screen in §4.6 and where the host counts are quoted in the §4.8 mini-case — so the inherited bound travels with the numbers rather than only with the Table 4-2 source row.

findings.chapter: Ch 3, §3.6.1 'Why the trend signal should not be read as "dense is dead"'
findings.evidence: "Qwen3.8-27B ([1P][FACT], model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B is a dense 27.8B model whose 4-bit weights fit on a single 24 GB consumer GPU, and Muse Glimmer 30B ([2°][FACT], source: vLLM-Recipes, citing the Meta model card) is a dense 29.6B local-agentic model..."
findings.issue: Unbalanced parenthesis: the '(' opened after 'Qwen3.8-27B' is never closed, so the source-citation parenthetical swallows the main clause ('is a dense 27.8B model...'). The parallel construction for 'Muse Glimmer 30B (...)' closes its parenthesis before 'is a dense 29.6B', confirming the intended closure point after the URL.
findings.fix_instruction: Insert the closing parenthesis after the model-card URL: 'Qwen3.8-27B ([1P][FACT], model card: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) is a dense 27.8B model...'.
